name: William Randolph Hearst

summary.text: Newspaper publisher William Randolph Hearst is credited in Billy Graham's own accounts and in later reporting with ordering his editors to 'Puff Graham' during the 1949 Los Angeles tent crusade, giving the campaign national exposure. Graham said he learned of the telegram from two of Hearst's sons; the two men never met.

sources.title: Stories inside that L.A. revival tent
Looking Back at the 1949 Los Angeles Crusade

facts.claim: Hearst is reported to have told his editors to 'Puff Graham' during the 1949 Los Angeles crusade; the Billy Graham Library says his newspapers gave the campaign national exposure and the crusade was extended from three weeks to eight.
facts.quote: his newspapers gave the campaign national exposure

sources.title: Looking Back at the 1949 Los Angeles Crusade
Stories inside that L.A. revival tent

facts.claim: Graham told the Los Angeles Times in 2004 that he heard of the 'Puff Graham' directive from two of Hearst's sons, and that Hearst and Graham never met.

sources.title: Stories inside that L.A. revival tent

facts.claim: A critical account by biographer Cecil Bothwell says Hearst contacted fellow publisher Henry Luce, and that Bernard Baruch arranged Luce's 1950 meeting with Graham in Columbia, South Carolina.
facts.quote: Bernard Baruch arranged a meeting between Luce and Graham while the preacher was staying with the segregationist Governor Strom Thurmond in the official mansion in Columbia

connections.claim: Hearst's newspapers promoted Graham's 1949 Los Angeles crusade after his reported 'Puff Graham' instruction (press backing, not a documented cash payment).

sources.title: Stories inside that L.A. revival tent
Looking Back at the 1949 Los Angeles Crusade

openQuestions: No primary document of the 'Puff Graham' telegram was found; the story rests on Graham's recollection of what Hearst's sons told him. No source shows Hearst money going to Graham.
